title: SDX accounts in a BRC-98 module (`p sdx`), secp256k1 operations: `k1key`, `k1peer`, `k1sign`, account and epoch selection, and rejections

citations.clause: Canonical derivation: one root for both curves
requirements K1-01, K1-02, K1-03, K1-04, K1-05

decisions.decision: `path` is the full SDX derivation identifier `2-<namespace>-<keyPath>`, used byte for byte with no Unicode normalisation. Its security level is 2, and its namespace is one the profile registers for the operation's curve (`wallets.profile.namespaces`). Nothing is derived under the rotation namespace. `decrypt` takes only paths in the encryption namespace, and `sign` and `k1sign` never take one. The key path is 1 to 1,033 bytes. For roles write, read, root and session it follows KEYS §1.6.1 with the profile's keywords and purposes: `account/<id>`, then `runtime/<id>`, then `action/<id>` with an optional `<purpose>/<id>` whose purpose the profile registers, or `session/<id>`. The delegation variant is refused. For role actor the only key path is `actor/<index>` under the delegation namespace, `<index>` decimal with no leading zero. `key` and `k1key` without `path` return the root public key with no derivation, and with `peer` and no `path` they are rejected. Every other operation that derives requires `path`.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Scheme, operations and carrier methods ("Namespace separation", "Key paths") and §Path scoping; KEYS §1.3 (key paths of 1 to 1033 bytes), §1.6.1 ("A <purpose> the validator does not recognise MUST be rejected at the derivation boundary"; one shared constant), §1.7 ("MUST NOT derive under a namespace absent from their deployment's profile"; the rotation role is reserved where rotation envelopes sign under the signing namespace, as KEYS §1.10.3 step 5 has them), §1.8.1, §1.11.2 ("The derivation library does not enforce the separation, so implementations MUST"), §1.12 item 10, §2.14.1.

decisions.decision: A child offset of 0 or >= n fails the derivation; it is never reduced mod n. This is a laboratory reading of a clause that contradicts itself.
decisions.basis: KEYS §1.8.2 computes the scalar as "int(hmac, big-endian) mod N" and then requires the derivation to fail when the scalar "is greater than or equal to N", which the reduction makes unreachable. KEYS §1.12 item 7 requires a known-answer test in which a scalar equal to N and one greater than N each raise the typed rejection, which only the unreduced value can give. The laboratory and sdx module draft statement §Canonical derivation step 3 apply the rule to the unreduced value.

decisions.decision: A seed outside [1, n - 1] makes the ikm unusable; it is never clamped. Both seeds are checked before either is used.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Canonical derivation step 2; KEYS §1.4.3.

decisions.decision: Test roots are fixed 64-byte ikm values: 0x00..0x3f (account 3MNQpxFAsp), 0x40..0x7f (recipient account 9VxTqR3mLp), 0x80..0xbf (the actor root), 0xc0..0xff (a session root); plus one searched ikm that is unusable. Account 5QkVr9TzWm has two epochs derived from the wallet root SHA-256 of a published label. They are public test key material, not secrets, never funded. The `wallets` table states which wallet holds which root.

The suite uses the laboratory deployment profile, fixtures/sdx/v1/deployment-profile.json, copied into `profile` and `wallets.profile`: format identifier `tpnil-sdx-lab:v1`, and SDX's example labels, namespaces, key-path keywords and purposes, for the laboratory only. One level-3 keyword, `action`, names a record on both curves: the P-256 signing key and recipient keys (ENV §8.5, §8.6) and the secp256k1 commitment key (ANC §3.1) of one record share the key path `account/<accountId>/runtime/<runtimeId>/action/<actionId>`.
decisions.basis: KEYS §1.3.1 (a deployment fixes and publishes its profile), §1.6.1 (a keyword is a profile value, and a profile "spells it that way everywhere"), §1.8.4 (the P-256 envelope signature and the secp256k1 transaction signature both use action/<actionId>), §1.11.2 (one key-path grammar on both curves); ANC §3.1; ENV §2.1. Source finding: ENV §8.5 and §8.6 write the record key path account/<account-id>/<writer-scope>/<writer-id>/record/<record-id> and make its segment literals profile parameters, while KEYS writes action; the laboratory reads the ENV literals as example values and fixes them to KEYS's words.

decisions.decision: The protocol name is `p sdx <operation> <role> <h>`. The logical protocol ID is exactly `<role> <h>`: `<role>` is one of write, read, root, actor and session, and `<h>` is the 32-character lowercase hex of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(UTF-8 accountId). Any other form is rejected.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Scheme, operations and carrier methods; BRC-98; BRC-229 Logical protocol ID.

decisions.decision: Roles write, read and root select the account whose tag is `<h>`, at epoch `ep`, or at the current epoch (the highest the wallet holds) when `ep` is absent; an unknown tag or epoch is rejected once the request is authorized (D-ERRORS). Role actor uses the wallet's actor root and role session the session root named by the `<sessionId>` segment that follows `/session/` in `path`; for both, `<h>` only scopes grants, and `ep` is rejected. A session request whose path names no session is rejected, and so is one without `path`. A path naming a session the wallet does not hold draws a fresh root (behavioural).
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Roots and selection. The draft does not say what a session request without a session in its path selects; the laboratory rejects it.

decisions.decision: `open` needs role `root` and a tag equal to tag(acct). For an epoch the wallet holds it returns R || K, 66 bytes, under a standing grant. For an account or epoch the wallet does not hold it derives the epoch from the wallet root with key ID "<acct> <ep>" and returns its R || K; creation always prompts, and the vectors mark the approved prompt with `prompt: "approve"`. Without `ep`, `open` of an unknown account creates epoch 0.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Roots and selection ("open"), §Permissions ("open prompts whenever it creates"), §Canonical derivation step 1.

decisions.decision: Each grant covers one [2, "p sdx <operation> <role> <h>"] for one originator and records the derivation-identifier prefixes it covers; the prompt shows them. A request whose `path` does not start with a covered prefix is rejected; a prefix that ends inside a key path ends with "/". A request without `path` needs only a grant for its protocol. Requests use security level 2 and counterparty `self`; `privileged: true` is rejected. Each operation and each account is granted separately. The vectors model grants in `wallets.entries.<wallet>.grants`.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Permissions ("Grant scope", "Account isolation", "Grant independence") and §Path scoping.

decisions.decision: Module calls use security level 2 and keyID "1". All requests come from one lab originator.

Error codes such as `scalar-rejected` and `point-x-range` are laboratory labels. The draft defines no codes; conformance requires the rejection, not the label. The laboratory checks in this order, so a module that checks in the same order gives the same label: the method and reserved names; the protocol name (scheme, operation, carrier method, security level, privileged, logical protocol ID); counterparty; the CBOR input (encoding, members, types, point validation, `hash` length, and the shape of `jwe` with its ephemeral key); `open`'s role and tag; the path: its form, a namespace registered for the curve, the rotation namespace, the encryption namespace for `decrypt`, `sign` and `k1sign`, the key path's length, then its grammar and purpose; the selection checks that read only the request (`ep` on the actor and session roles, the session a path names); the grant and its prefixes, or the approved prompt, which `open` needs whenever it creates; root selection from what the wallet holds (account, epoch, a tag another account holds, a wallet that cannot create); derivation; then, for `decrypt`, the JOSE steps. Checks that read what the wallet holds come after authorization, so a request with no grant and no approval is refused alike whether or not the wallet holds its account or epoch.
decisions.basis: Lab decision. The order of authorization and root selection follows sdx module draft statement §Permissions and §Errors.

decisions.decision: secp256k1 child keys are BRC-42 on the selected root k = secp256k1_seed: S = compressed(k·Q) with Q = `peer` or k·G for self, h = HMAC-SHA-256(S, UTF-8(path)) read big-endian, rejected when 0 or >= n; `k1key` returns (k + h)·G and `k1peer` Q + h·G. Each result equals stock BRC-100 getPublicKey of a wallet whose root is k, with protocol [s, <namespace>] and key ID <keyPath> read from the derivation identifier, counterparty `self` or the peer's hex, and forSelf true for `k1key`; without `path`, `k1key` equals that wallet's identity key. The generator fails if @bsv/sdk 4.0.1 ProtoWallet gives any other value, and each case records the stock call in `brc100`.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Canonical derivation step 3 ("On secp256k1, SDX's derivation identifier is a BRC-43 invoice number"); KEYS §1.8.1, §1.8.2; BRC-42; BRC-43.

decisions.decision: `k1sign` signs the 32 bytes of `hash` as given, with no further hashing, using the own child key, an RFC 6979 nonce (HMAC-SHA-256, h1 = hash mod n) and low-S canonicalisation, and returns the DER encoding with no sighash byte. The result equals stock BRC-100 createSignature with `hashToDirectlySign` on the same derivation, recorded in `brc100`. It signs under the signing namespace (chain tips and top-up outputs) and the handoff namespace (handoff outputs addressed to the account).
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Canonical derivation step 4 and the `k1sign` row; KEYS §1.6.1, §1.7, §1.8.3; RFC 6979 §3.2.

decisions.decision: `peer` in `k1key`, `k1peer` and `k1sign` is validated on secp256k1 before any multiplication: exactly 33 bytes, prefix 02 or 03, x < p on the encoded integer before any reducing parser, on y² = x³ + 7.
decisions.basis: sdx module draft statement §Point validation; BRC-229.

decisions.decision: An offset of 0, n or more cannot be found by search on secp256k1 (probability about 2^-128), so case offset-range-secp256k1 pins KEYS §1.12 item 7 as a computation on injected values: 0, n, n + 1 and 2^256 - 1 are refused and 1 and n - 1 accepted. VC-P256 pins the same rule through module requests with a P-256 offset above n found by search. No case asks a module for a test hook.

The commitment key path is `account/<accountId>/runtime/<runtimeId>/action/<actionId>` under the signing namespace, counterparty self (ANC §3.1, KEYS §1.6.1 level 3), the same derivation identifier as the record's P-256 signing key. The handoff lock is level-4 purpose `handoff` with `<refIdHex>` under `sdx handoff`, counterparty the recipient's secp256k1 root. The top-up lock is purpose `topup`, ordinal 0, under the signing namespace.

Case k1sign-commitment-spend carries synthetic version-1 transactions: `previous` has the record output (ANC §2.1 container with the commitment key, 1 satoshi), and `spending` spends it with lock time 0 and sequence 0xffffffff. `hash` is SHA-256d of the SIGHASH_ALL|FORKID (0x41) preimage of input 0, and the unlocking script pushes the k1sign result followed by 0x41. Nothing is broadcast.
decisions.basis: ANC §2.1, §3.1; sdx module draft statement §How SDX uses it ("Spend the chain's tip").

decisions.decision: A module case is executable: load `wallets.entries[case.wallet]`, send `request.method` with `request.args`, and compare the result with `expected.ciphertext`, or confirm a rejection when `expected.error` is set. `variants` repeat the request with the listed argument overrides. Point-rejection cases list one request per position. No case needs a test hook in the module.

profile.note: The laboratory deployment profile, copied from `file` (KEYS §1.3.1; ENV §2.1), LAB_SELF_TEST_ONLY. The labels, namespaces, key-path keywords, purposes and credential type are SDX's example values, used for the laboratory only; the format identifier is the laboratory's own. One level-3 keyword, `action`, names a record on both curves (decision D-PROFILE). `actor` is also the keyword of the actor's persistent key path `actor/<index>` (module draft, step 1). The credential type is not an input to any case of this suite. The identifiers are the worked example of KEYS §1.8.1.

testKeys.note: Public test key material, not a secret, never funded. Each root is a fixed 64-byte ikm. LAB_SELF_TEST_ONLY.

wallets.note: Wallet state for replay. Every module case names one wallet and starts from the state below; no case sees another case's effects. An account epoch is either an `ikm` (64 bytes, imported or fixed) or `{walletRoot, derived: true}`: its ikm is derived from that wallet root with `walletRootDerivation` and key ID "<acct> <ep>". `current` is the epoch used when a request carries no `ep`. `actor` is the wallet's actor root, and `sessions` maps a session ID (the hex `<sessionId>` segment of a session path) to that session's root. `R` and `K` are the P-256 and secp256k1 root public keys of each root, for checking a loaded state. `grants` are the standing grants of the one laboratory originator: a request reaches derivation only under a grant whose protocolID equals its own and, when it carries `path`, under one of its derivation-identifier prefixes. A case with `prompt: "approve"` runs as if the user approved the prompt the request raises.

generator.deterministic: Every value except the JWEs that `decrypt` cases open is regenerated byte for byte by `node generate.mjs --check`.

frozen.parts: The JWEs that `decrypt` cases open, made by jose 5.10.0 GeneralEncrypt with a random content-encryption key, IV and ephemeral key per recipient, and stored with the protected header, recipient kids and plaintext they were made for and their content-encryption key. They were generated once and are re-verified by decryption, with jose and with node:crypto, on every run.

oracles.coverage: Every case, through the module semantics of src/sdx/p256.mjs. OpenSSL performs scalar multiplication and HMAC; src/sdx/ec-p256.mjs adds point validation and addition; src/sdx/brc42.mjs independently recomputes every BRC-100 getPublicKey result; src/sdx/tx.mjs recomputes the transaction preimage and evaluates the spend. RFC 6979 nonces are recomputed with node:crypto HMAC.
Every value: child keys, BRC-100 results, RFC 6979 nonces, DER signatures and their verification, injected offsets, request rules and the transaction preimage hash.

cases.title: `k1key` without `path` returns the account's secp256k1 root public key K = secp256k1_seed·G, with no derivation; stock BRC-100 returns it as the identity key of a wallet whose root is that seed

`k1key`: the commitment key of a record output, ANC §3.1's self-derivation under the signing namespace on the path `account/<accountId>/runtime/<runtimeId>/action/<actionId>`: the same derivation identifier as the record's P-256 signing key in VC-P256, on the other curve (KEYS §1.8.4, §1.11.2)
The same request with role `read` selects the same account root and returns the same key; keyID selects nothing
`k1key` with `peer` set to the account's own secp256k1 root equals `k1key` without `peer` (self)
`k1key`: a funding top-up output lock at level-4 purpose `topup`, ordinal 0 (KEYS §1.6.1)
`k1peer`: the writer locks a handoff output to the recipient account's secp256k1 root under `sdx handoff`, so only that recipient can spend it (KEYS §1.6.1, §1.7)
`k1key` with `peer`: the recipient, under its own account tag, derives the same handoff key from its own root and the writer's root (counterparty symmetry, KEYS §1.12 item 5)
`k1key` without `path` and role `actor`: the actor root's secp256k1 public key
`k1key` with role `actor`: the secp256k1 key at the actor's persistent path `2-sdx delegate-actor/0`, the key a grant records as `actorPubKey_k1` when the actor publishes one (KEYS §2.3)
`k1key` with role `session`: the session root named by the path's sessionId gives the session's secp256k1 key (KEYS §2.14.2)
`k1sign`: the account spends its chain tip. `hash` is the SIGHASH_ALL|FORKID signature hash of input 0 of the next record's transaction, and the key is the tip's commitment key (ANC §2.1, §3.1)

transaction.note: Synthetic transactions; nothing is broadcast. `previous` carries the record output (output 0, 1 satoshi) and `spending` spends it with the k1sign result followed by the sighash byte 0x41.

cases.given: No grant exists for the originator and [2, "p sdx k1sign write 1f520702ec75fa65f6048ccdf8ce3efe"].
cases.then: The call fails and no prompt is shown.

cases.title: The `sign` grant does not satisfy it; each operation is granted separately (request vector k1-no-grant-from-sign).
cases.given: A grant exists for [2, "p sdx sign write 1f520702ec75fa65f6048ccdf8ce3efe"].
cases.when: The application calls `k1sign` under the same logical protocol ID.
cases.then: The `sign` grant does not satisfy it; each operation is granted separately (request vector k1-no-grant-from-sign).

cases.title: The grant does not satisfy it (request vector k1-account-isolation).
cases.given: A grant exists for [2, "p sdx k1sign write 1f520702ec75fa65f6048ccdf8ce3efe"].
cases.when: The application calls `k1sign` with the tag of 5QkVr9TzWm.
cases.then: The grant does not satisfy it (request vector k1-account-isolation).
